endorsements.quote: Verify every drug dose, antibiotic, and threshold against your formulary and unit protocol before acting.
The AI assisted; the clinician decided.
Document that a named clinician made the decision.
Third, responsible adoption requires more than a framework.
Provide structured clinician training and competency assessment (see the proposed NeonatAIlogy curriculum).
Second, tell the AI what it cannot do - for example, “do not prescribe; rank differentials only” - because limiting scope reduces the range of possible hallucination.
Explicitly limiting the role reduces hallucination risk.

unlisted_practices: Define one bounded clinical task per AI interaction rather than open-ended queries.
Anonymize clinical inputs and never enter patient identifiers into any LLM.
Use only enterprise-grade LLM platforms meeting data-protection standards such as HIPAA or GDPR for any input containing clinical detail.
Obtain information-governance and data-protection sign-off before entering clinical detail into an AI tool.
Secure parental consent or information-sharing arrangements for AI-assisted care before bedside use.
Require a senior clinician to confirm before any drug, procedure, or escalation based on AI output.
Treat every AI output as advisory only and cross-reference against current guidelines.
Seek calibration data (e.g., Brier score) and external validation in a comparable population before adopting predictive ML models.
Perform local validation before any AI tool enters clinical use.
Establish an AI clinical safety board, an AI registry, and mandatory near-miss reporting.
Maintain an AI near-miss log recording platform, task, error type, and outcome.
Ask the AI to state uncertainty, cite sources, and give evidence grades, and treat ungradable output with skepticism.
Do not adopt the GIRISH framework as unit policy until validated; confine use to education and governed evaluation.
Provide open-source, low-bandwidth, enterprise-grade AI options for LMIC NICUs rather than substituting less-safe consumer tools.
Obtain local institutional oversight or ethics committee approval before structured use of prompt templates in patient care.
